title: intentd: the Intent daemon, and a menubar app that controls it
objective: `intentd` is the Intent daemon -- Rust, shipped in the keg beside `intent` -- and this thread owns its lifecycle surface and a macOS menubar app that controls it, in the pattern hv set with Conflab and now Geodica. Opened by vc on hv's instruction 2026-08-26; scope and sequencing are hv's ("that's for when we get to intentd").
body:
## Status

Triage. No work is scheduled; WP-01 carries a drop-in design so the work can start without a discovery phase when hv calls it.

## Relations

- ST0057 WP-07 defines `intent://` addressing and read resolution; the app's URL-scheme handler is a client of it, never a second resolver.
- `intentd` today: built from `native/rust/crates/intentd`, installed by the tap formula beside `intent` (`libexec/bin/intentd`; executable since 3.0.0 `revision 1`).

wps.title: Menubar app: control of intentd after Geodica's design -- no product logic, every control an intent verb, the daemon is the authority on the daemon
wps.objective: **A Swift menubar app that shows `intentd`'s state, starts, stops and restarts it, tails its log in a terminal-styled console, holds preferences, and handles an `intent://` URL scheme -- holding NO product logic.** Every control is an `intent` / `intentd` verb it shells out to; every fact it displays comes from the daemon's status endpoint or the CLI; nothing in Swift knows a log format, a pidfile layout or a config schema. Geodica's app is the drop-in example, used more or less as-is with Intent-specific tweaks (hv, 2026-08-26).
wps.body:
## The example, verbatim

`design-menubar-app.md` beside this thread is the Geodica handoff as received from `geodica-7f` on 2026-08-26: design, console, the tail-orphan trap, the build pipeline, settings, icon semantics. Geodica's own sources: `Dropbox/Geodica/_tools/design/closed/008-menubar-app.md`, `_tools/docs/app.md`, `_tools/bin/geodica_app`, `_tools/native/macos/Geodica/`.

## Intent-specific tweaks (the whole of the delta)

- **Status endpoint on `intentd`**: `GET /_status` returning JSON (pid, version, source commit, started_at, uptime, the projects it serves); the app polls it and derives running / degraded / stopped. The daemon is the authority on the daemon.
- **The tail-orphan trap, checked first**: if `intentd`'s log path is a pipeline behind a runtime, the verb takes its own process group down when its stdin closes, verified against SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGKILL, BEFORE any console is built on it (`ps -A | grep tail` after a few ctrl-c's).
- **`intent://` URL scheme**: the handler resolves an `intent://` address through ST0057 WP-07's read resolution and opens it via `intent edit`.
- **Build pipeline as a devbin verb** (`int app build|run|test|install|uninstall|start|stop|status|icons`): xcodegen from `project.yml`; version, commit and source-tree hash passed as BUILD SETTINGS into Info.plist, never a generated Swift file; `status` compares the installed bundle's source-tree hash to the working tree; `run` execs the built binary rather than `open`; `lsappinfo`, not `pgrep`; `SYMROOT` / `OBJROOT` pinned so nothing lands on a synced tree.
- **PATH**: captured once from the login shell at launch and handed to every child; the CLI resolved through it with a Locate... override; nothing baked into the bundle.
- **Icon**: tinted only when the daemon is REACHABLE, template-rendered otherwise, orange for the transient; glyph drawn with gaps; rasterised with `rsvg-convert`.
- **Brand tokens**: Intent's own, not Geodica's ink / bone / accent.

## Not in scope until hv says

The daemon's own feature surface; where the app's sources live (a crate-adjacent `native/macos/Intent/`, mirroring Geodica, is the obvious home); a Homebrew cask.

criteria.text: **THE APP HOLDS NO PRODUCT LOGIC: EVERY CONTROL IS A VERB IT SHELLS OUT TO, AND NOTHING IN SWIFT KNOWS A LOG FORMAT, A PIDFILE LAYOUT OR A CONFIG SCHEMA.** hv set this as the whole shape of the app on 2026-08-26 and it is the row every other row on this thread leans on: start, stop, restart and doctor are `intent` / `intentd` invocations, and every fact displayed comes from the daemon or the CLI rather than from a Swift-side derivation. **The check is by ABSENCE and it is mechanical**: the Swift sources contain no parser for a log line, no path assembled toward a pidfile, and no key read out of a config file. **The daemon is the authority on the daemon** -- an app that computes any of the three has taken a second home for a value `intentd` already owns, and the two will disagree at exactly the moment the app exists to be trusted.

**THE APP'S HEALTH PREDICATE AND THE CLI'S ROUTING PREDICATE ARE ONE PREDICATE, NOT TWO THAT AGREE.** `AC-08.3` rules how a client decides the daemon is live: a completed request-response round-trip under a bounded deadline, never a presence test and never a bare `connect()`. **The app asks the same question and MUST reach the same answer through the same code path** -- the CLI verb, not a Swift reimplementation of the probe. **Two homes for `is intentd running` is the defect this estate has now recorded at three scales**, and this is its worst instance, because the disagreement is SILENT AND INVERTED: the menubar shows a green dot while the CLI routes every verb in-process, and the operator is looking at the one surface built to tell them otherwise.

**THE APP TALKS GRAPHQL/JSON TO `intentd` AND NOTHING ELSE, PER `D56`, AND THE `GET /_status` IN THIS WP'S BODY IS SUPERSEDED BY THIS ROW.** hv, 2026-08-29: *the macOS app (Swift) and the cli (rust) need to talk GraphQL to intentd (rust)*; `D56` gives the daemon ONE output contract, GraphQL/JSON over the socket and over HTTP, and the deciding argument for that reversal was this very app -- a SwiftUI menubar cannot consume HTML. **The body of WP-01 still names `GET /_status` returning JSON**, carried in verbatim from the Geodica handoff on 2026-08-26, three days before the ruling that removed it. **It is named here rather than quietly dropped, because a superseded design that stays legible in the artefact gets built from**: the handoff is the drop-in example and a reader following it lands on the endpoint that no longer exists. **Status is a query like every other query**, and `stopped` is derived from that query failing rather than reported by a lighter endpoint that would be a second home for the same fact and could answer while the real surface cannot.

**THE TAIL-ORPHAN TRAP IS VERIFIED BEFORE ANY CONSOLE IS BUILT ON IT, AGAINST SIGTERM, SIGINT AND SIGKILL SEPARATELY.** Geodica's handoff names this first and the ordering is the point: if the log verb is a pipeline behind a runtime, it takes its own process group down when its stdin closes, and a console built on top of that leaks a `tail` per open-and-close. **Checked by driving the app open and shut several times and then reading `ps`**, not by reasoning about the pipeline. **The three signals are checked SEPARATELY because they do not share a path**: a handler that cleans up on SIGTERM and SIGINT proves nothing about SIGKILL, which cannot be handled at all, so the orphan must be prevented by process-group construction rather than by a shutdown hook. **A leaked tail is invisible to the operator and unbounded in count** -- the failure is that the machine gets slower over a week and nothing ever points at the menubar.

**THE `intent://` HANDLER RESOLVES THROUGH ST0057 WP-07'S READ RESOLUTION AND IS NEVER A SECOND RESOLVER.** The URL scheme is a CLIENT of the addressing rules, so the app parses no address itself: it hands the URL to the resolver and opens what comes back via `intent edit`. **An address that resolves in the CLI and not in the app, or to a different entity, is a failure of this row and not a difference of opinion** -- and the `0149` defect is the standing reminder of how that decays, where `intent edit issue 148` parsed the kind correctly, discarded it, and refused about a steel thread the caller never named. **A resolver reached from two places drifts at whichever one is edited second**, which is a property of the arrangement rather than of anyone's care.

**THE APP DISTINGUISHES THE SAME THREE ENDPOINT STATES THE ROUTING RULE DOES -- LIVE, STALE, ABSENT -- AND NEVER RENDERS `RUNNING` FOR AN ENDPOINT THAT CONNECTS WITHOUT ANSWERING.** `AC-08.3` names both false positives and this row inherits both: **a dead daemon leaves its socket file behind**, and **an inherited listening descriptor accepts connections nothing will ever answer** (no atomic `SOCK_CLOEXEC` on macOS; measured by cc 2026-08-29 at 1 in 300 with a sibling thread spawning children, 0 in 2000 without). **The app is where these are most damaging, because it is the surface an operator consults INSTEAD of measuring**, so a green dot is trusted in a way a CLI exit code is not. **Both states are constructed in the check, never waited for** -- a suite that passes because a 1-in-300 race did not fire has measured nothing.

**THE BUILD, RUN, TEST AND INSTALL PIPELINE IS A DEVBIN VERB RATHER THAN A SEQUENCE ANYONE REMEMBERS**, and the shipped artefact is signed and notarised per `D38` on the `int macos sign|notarize|verify` path that `AC-11.1` already established. **`D38` requires both, unconditionally**, and the app is the first artefact on this estate where the operator meets Gatekeeper directly: an unnotarised menubar app does not fail loudly, it fails as a dialog the user cannot get past, on a machine the developer does not own. **The verb is the deliverable, not the invocation it wraps** -- the same argument that put `int macos ...` ahead of cargo-dist, which signs only and does not notarise at all.

**THE ICON IS INTENT'S TURTLE (`docs/design/intent-logo.*`) AND ITS STATE SEMANTICS ARE DERIVED FROM THE HEALTH PREDICATE, NEVER STORED ALONGSIDE IT.** hv named the asset and the reason on 2026-08-26 -- *slow and steady wins the race* -- and the substantive half of this row is the second clause: the menubar glyph is a RENDERING of the one predicate in `AC-01.2`, computed at paint time, with no cached `lastKnownState` that can outlive what produced it. **A status cached beside the thing it describes is the gate-figure defect in miniature**: two homes, one value, and the stale one is the one on screen.

**THE APP RESOLVES `intent` THROUGH A CAPTURED LOGIN-SHELL PATH, BECAUSE A `.app` BUNDLE HAS NO LOGIN SHELL AND THEREFORE NO PATH.** Every child the app spawns is handed that environment, and binary resolution falls back to it. **One home for the shell-out** -- a single CLI wrapper owning binary resolution, environment and error mapping, with nothing else in the app spawning anything -- which is `AC-01.1`'s no-product-logic rule in the one place it is easy to breach twice.

**THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE IT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL A USER REPORTS IT, AND THEN IT IS UNFALSIFIABLE FROM THE DEVELOPER'S SIDE.** The app cannot find `intent` while the user's terminal can, on a machine the developer does not own, with no error that names the cause. **Priced by ic on 2026-08-30 from Geodica's `LoginShell.swift`, 96 lines that exist for exactly this** -- a cost nobody discovers by reasoning about the design and nobody would put in an estimate without having read the source. **A homebrew-installed `intent` under `/opt/homebrew/bin` is not on a bundle's default `PATH`**, so this is the ordinary case rather than an edge one.

**Asserted by launching the built bundle with a deliberately minimal environment**, never by running the app from a terminal that already carries the developer's `PATH` -- which is the instrument that cannot fail, on the one axis this row is about.

attachments.text:
# Design handoff: a macOS menubar app with a terminal-styled console (from Geodica)

Received by vc from the Geodica `_tools` session (`geodica-7f`) at 2026-08-26 14:51Z, at hv's request: hv wants Intent to have the equivalent and will liaise on what to do with it and where it should live. Parked here verbatim so it survives the session; NOT a work item until hv says so. Questions go back to `geodica-7f`.

---

WHAT WE BUILT

Geodica has a local CMS daemon (`geodica cms serve`, Elixir/Bandit on :4360). It now also has `~/Applications/Geodica.app`: a Swift menubar app that shows the daemon's state, starts/stops it, tails its log in a console window, holds preferences, and handles a custom `geodica://` URL scheme. ~1,900 lines of Swift. The design doc is `Dropbox/Geodica/_tools/design/closed/008-menubar-app.md` and the user-facing guide is `_tools/docs/app.md`; the code is `_tools/native/macos/Geodica/`.

THE LOAD-BEARING PRINCIPLE

The app holds NO product logic. Every control is a CLI verb it shells out to; every fact it displays comes from the daemon or the CLI. Start/Stop/Restart run `geodica cms serve` / `--stop`; "Rebuild index" runs a verb; the console is literally a child `geodica cms logs` streamed into a text view. Nothing in Swift knows the log format, the pidfile layout or the config schema. That is what keeps a GUI from becoming a second implementation that drifts. For Intent the same rule would be: the app runs `intent` subcommands and renders their output, nothing more.

The one thing it reads directly is a status endpoint we added to the daemon: `GET /_status` returns JSON -- site, port, pid, version, started_at, uptime_s, requests answered, mounts, search-index state. The app polls it every 5s with a 1.5s timeout and derives running / degraded (answers but not with /_status -- an old daemon) / stopped (connection refused). The daemon is the authority on the daemon. If Intent has no daemon, the equivalent is a `--json` status verb.

THE CONSOLE (the bit Matthew called "excellent")

An NSWindow holding an NSTextView in an NSScrollView, styled from our brand tokens: ink ground (#0E141F), bone text (#F5F2E7) at 85%, request lines at 55%, errors and markers in the accent (#CD285E), IBM Plex Mono 12 with a system-monospace fallback. Footer bar: **Verbose** checkbox, **Follow** checkbox, **Clear** (also Cmd-K), **Copy**, and the path being tailed. Window title carries the log file name. Cmd-L toggles it; closing it ends the tail.

Details that made it feel right:

- Verbose toggles by killing the child and re-running the verb with `--verbose`. The filter lives in the CLI, never duplicated in Swift.
- Follow auto-scrolls, clears itself when the user scrolls up (observe `NSScrollView.didLiveScrollNotification`, compare visible maxY to frame maxY), and re-arms at the bottom.
- One-off commands (doctor, index rebuild, a URL click) stream into the SAME view between accent-coloured markers: `>> geodica doctor` ... output ... `>> exit 0 - 3.4s`. One place to look for everything the app did. One command at a time; a second request is refused with an alert, not queued.
- A 5,000-line ring buffer. When it trims N lines the view deletes the same N leading lines from its text storage, so the two never diverge.
- Line classification is a pure function over the text (marker / error / warning / request / log) -- trivially unit-testable, and the only thing Swift assumes about the log.

THE TRAP YOU WILL HIT -- this cost us the most time

Killing the tail child does not work the way you expect. Our `cms logs` is `tail -f | grep` under `sh`, under the BEAM, under a bash dispatcher. `Process.terminate()` from Swift reaches only the top of that chain and leaves orphaned tails behind. Worse, we discovered the CLI verb had been leaking a tail on EVERY exit, including plain ctrl-c at a terminal, because the BEAM starts port programs in their own process group so no signal ever reached them.

The fix belongs in the CLI, not the app: the verb runs its pipeline under a shell that reads its own stdin and takes the process group down when that pipe closes -- the runtime's death closes it, however it dies. Verified against SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGKILL: zero orphans, where every previous run leaked one. Then the app needs no special handling at all -- plain terminate() works. If Intent's log tailing is a pipeline behind a runtime, check for this before you build any UI on top of it; `ps -A | grep tail` after a few ctrl-c's will tell you in seconds.

THE BUILD PIPELINE

No hand-edited Xcode project: `project.yml` + xcodegen generates the `.xcodeproj` (which we track so Xcode opens it directly). One CLI verb, `geodica app`, owns everything -- `build` (regenerates the project only when the spec or the SET OF SOURCE FILES changed, since xcodegen scans sources by presence and a new file otherwise silently isn't in the project), `run`, `test`, `install`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `icons`.

Four things worth stealing verbatim:

1. Version/commit/source-tree are passed to xcodebuild as BUILD SETTINGS and substituted into Info.plist -- not written into a generated Swift file. The generated-file approach has a well-known failure where the build phase is skipped by dependency analysis and the app ships stamped with a commit it was not built from.
2. `status` compares the installed bundle's source-tree hash against the working tree and says "stale -- reinstall". That line is repeated in `doctor`.
3. `run` execs the built binary directly rather than `open`ing the bundle: LaunchServices resolves `open` by bundle id and will cheerfully launch an INSTALLED copy instead of the one you just built. Similarly `status`/`stop` use `lsappinfo info -only pid <bundle-id>`, not `pgrep` -- children of a hardened-runtime app cannot see it in the process table, so a pgrep shelled from inside the app reports it dead.
4. Pin `SYMROOT` and `OBJROOT` on the command line, not just `-derivedDataPath`. An Xcode "Locations -> Custom, relative to workspace" preference otherwise puts products next to the project; ours landed on a Dropbox tree and codesign died on synced extended attributes ("resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed").

A GUI app also launches with a bare PATH and none of your environment. We capture the login shell's PATH once at launch (`/bin/zsh -ilc 'printf %s "$PATH"; command -v <cli>'`, ~0.15s) and hand it to every child, and resolve the CLI binary through it with a symlink fallback and a Locate... override in settings. Nothing is baked into the bundle.

SETTINGS + THE REST

Tabbed NSWindow of NSGridView panels in the System Settings register (right-aligned labels, left-aligned controls, hint rows under each). Four tabs: General (launch at login via SMAppService, registered on first run; start-the-daemon-at-launch; console-on-run), Daemon (the status rows plus lifecycle buttons; config file shown as a path with Edit.../Reveal -- the app never WRITES what the CLI reads), Estate/Paths (everything as resolved, with Reveal buttons), About (the build stamps).

Menubar icon: we tint it with the brand accent when the daemon is REACHABLE and leave it template-rendered (adapts black/white to the bar) when it is not, with orange for the transient. The obvious alternative -- tint the failure red -- makes an idle daemon look like an alarm, and leaves "running", the state you are in all day, looking like every other template glyph. Also: an icon that is a set of OVERLAPPING shapes flattens to a silhouette blob at 18px; we redrew the glyph with gaps. And use `rsvg-convert`, not `qlmanage`, to rasterise -- QuickLook flattens transparency to white, which a template image renders as a solid square.

One last thing worth copying: we put a small on/off switch in the WEB app's header that starts and stops the menubar app (state from `/_status`, click POSTs a whitelisted action). The two surfaces can each recover the other.

Files to read if useful: `_tools/design/closed/008-menubar-app.md` (design + a closing note with measurements and everything that went wrong), `_tools/docs/app.md`, `_tools/bin/geodica_app`, `_tools/native/macos/Geodica/Geodica/Views/Console/ConsoleWindowController.swift` and `Services/ConsoleRunner.swift`.
